descripcion_es: Everyday actions, the home and free time.
resumen: Verbs and expressions to talk about what you do on a normal day, housework and your hobbies, with adverbs of frequency.

explicacion.texto: We talk about routines in the present simple (I get up at seven; she gets up at eight). Many daily actions are fixed expressions with have, do, make or go: it is a good idea to learn them as a whole.

filas: I have a shower every morning.
eat the morning / midday / evening meal (es: desayunar / comer / cenar)
travel to your job / school (es: ir al trabajo / colegio)
He goes to work by bus.
arrive at your house (es: llegar a casa)
I get home at about six.
I usually go to bed at eleven.
clean and tidy the house (es: hacer las tareas de casa)
wash the dishes (es: fregar los platos)
buy food for the house (es: hacer la compra)
I do the shopping on Saturdays.
tidy the sheets on your bed (es: hacer la cama)
prepare the evening meal (es: hacer la cena)
Who makes dinner at your house?
put the rubbish outside (es: sacar la basura)
Can you take out the rubbish?
every time / most times / many times (es: siempre / normalmente / a menudo)
some times / not often / at no time (es: a veces / rara vez / nunca)
each day / one time each week (es: todos los días / una vez a la semana)
I go swimming twice a week.
when I am not working or studying (es: en mi tiempo libre)
In my free time I read.
walk for pleasure (es: dar un paseo)
look at the television / a series (es: ver la tele / una serie)
We watch a series after dinner.
spend time with friends, informal (es: quedar con amigos)
I hang out with friends on Fridays.

items: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb (I often cook) but after be (I'm always tired).

Do is used for tasks (do homework, do the ironing); make, for creating or preparing something (make a cake, make dinner). Make the bed is a fixed expression that does not follow this logic: learn it as a block.
With home you don't use to: go home, get home.

ejemplos.frase: On weekdays I get up at seven and have a quick breakfast.
ejemplos.traduccion: Entre semana me levanto a las siete y desayuno rápido.

ejemplos.frase: My partner does the cooking and I do the washing-up.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mi pareja cocina y yo friego los platos.

ejemplos.frase: We rarely eat out during the week.
ejemplos.traduccion: Rara vez comemos fuera entre semana.

ejemplos.frase: In my free time I play the guitar.
ejemplos.traduccion: En mi tiempo libre toco la guitarra.

ejemplos.frase: She goes to the gym three times a week.
ejemplos.traduccion: Va al gimnasio tres veces por semana.

ejemplos.frase: I'm always tired on Monday mornings.
ejemplos.traduccion: Siempre estoy cansado los lunes por la mañana.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I go to home at six.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Home does not take to after go, come or get.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I make my homework after school.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I do my homework after school.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Homework and tasks go with do.
With be, the adverb of frequency goes after the verb.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I take a shower in the night.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I have/take a shower at night.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “por la noche” is at night.

ejercicios.frase: Can you ___ the bed before you leave?
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit explains that do is used for tasks and make for creating or preparing something, and adds that make the bed is a fixed expression. The clue is the bed: we always say make the bed, even though it is a household task. That is why it is the exception you need to memorise.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “hacer la cama” is make the bed.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Puedes hacer la cama antes de irte?

errores_previstos.explicacion: Although it is a task, the fixed expression is make the bed; we don't say do the bed.
Fix means repair; the expression is make the bed.

ejercicios.frase: I ___ the shopping on Saturday mornings.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in this unit applies: tasks go with do. The clue is the shopping: buying food is a normal household task, like do the housework or do the washing-up. So it is I do the shopping, in the present simple because it is a habit.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “hacer la compra” is do the shopping.
ejercicios.traduccion: Hago la compra los sábados por la mañana.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Make is used for creating or preparing something; the shopping is a task, so it goes with do.
We say go shopping, without the; with the shopping the verb is do.

ejercicios.frase: I wake ___ at six but I don't get up until half past.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit distinguishes wake up (stop sleeping) and get up (leave your bed). The clue is the contrast in the sentence: first she wakes up and half an hour later she gets up. The complete phrasal verb is wake up, so the particle up is missing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me despierto a las seis, pero no me levanto hasta las seis y media.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Wake on does not exist; the verb is wake up.
A calque of the Spanish reflexive “me despierto”; wake up does not take a pronoun.

glosario.definicion_l: cause to become awake or conscious · stop sleeping
rise to one's feet · get up and out of bed

ejercicios.frase: Please take ___ the rubbish; the bin is full.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit includes take out the rubbish (Spanish “sacar la basura”). The clue is the reason, “the bin is full”: you need to take the rubbish outside. The particle out expresses movement outwards. In American English you say take out the trash or the garbage.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “sacar la basura” is take out the rubbish.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por favor, saca la basura; el cubo está lleno.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Take off means to remove clothes or (for a plane) to leave the ground; for rubbish it is take out.
Take away means to carry something away; for rubbish the fixed expression is take out.

glosario.definicion_l: an identification number consisting of a two-part code assigned to banks and savings associations; the first part shows the location and the second… · a container; usually has a lid

ejercicios.frase: We usually ___ dinner at about nine.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit gives have breakfast, lunch and dinner for the meals of the day. The clue is dinner: meals go with have. Spanish says “cenar” or “tomar la cena”, but in English you don't use take or do. Usually goes before the main verb, as the unit says.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Meals go with have: have dinner.

por_opcion.have: Correct: have dinner means eat the evening meal; meals go with have.
por_opcion.take: Incorrect: take dinner is a calque of Spanish “tomar”; it is not used with meals.
por_opcion.do: Incorrect: do does not go with meals; do dinner is informal and means to organise a dinner, not to eat dinner.

ejercicios.frase: I don't like going out. I ___ go to parties.
ejercicios.explicacion: This practises the adverbs of frequency in the unit. The clue is the first sentence, “I don't like going out”: someone who doesn't like going out doesn't go to parties often. Rarely means “not often” and goes before the main verb: I rarely go.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If you don't like going out, you go rarely: rarely.
ejercicios.traduccion: No me gusta salir. Rara vez voy a fiestas.

por_opcion.rarely: Correct: rarely (“not often”) fits with not liking going out.
por_opcion.always: Incorrect: always (“every time”) contradicts the first sentence.
por_opcion.usually: Incorrect: usually (“most times”) also contradicts not liking going out.

glosario.definicion_l: move out of or depart from · leave the house to go somewhere

ejercicios.frase: What time do you get ___ in the evening?
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit says that with home you don't use to: go home, get home. The clue is get followed by home with the meaning “arrive at your house”. Here home works as an adverb of place, so it doesn't need a preposition. At home means “in your house”, a state, not arriving.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Arrive at your house is get home, with no preposition.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿A qué hora llegas a casa por la tarde?

por_opcion.home: Correct: get home, with no preposition, means arrive at your house.
por_opcion.to home: Incorrect: home does not take to after go, come or get.
por_opcion.at home: Incorrect: at home means “in your house” (be at home); get at home does not mean arrive.

ejercicios.frase: She goes swimming ___ a week: on Tuesdays and Fridays.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit includes expressions like once a week and twice a week. The clue is “on Tuesdays and Fridays”: two days, that is, two times. In English “one time” is once and “two times” is twice; from three on we say three times.
ejercicios.traduccion: Va a nadar dos veces por semana: los martes y los viernes.

por_opcion.two: Incorrect: two is the number; you would need two times, which is less common than twice.
por_opcion.second: Incorrect: second is the ordinal number (2nd).

glosario.definicion_l: two times · to double the degree
on one occasion · as soon as

ejercicios.frase: I always am hungry after work.
respuestas: I am always hungry after work.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit says that adverbs of frequency go after be. The clue is the verb am: with be, the adverb always goes after the verb, not before it. So it is I am always hungry, or I'm always hungry. With other verbs it does go before (I always eat).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With be, the adverb goes after the verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: Siempre tengo hambre después del trabajo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I always am hungry after work.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence without the correction: with be, the adverb goes after it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Always I am hungry after work.
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish word order; always does not usually go at the start of a sentence like this.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I am hungry always after work.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The adverb doesn't go after the adjective; it goes between be and hungry.

ejercicios.frase: My children make their homework in the kitchen.
respuestas: My children do their homework in the kitchen.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in this unit applies: tasks, and homework in particular, go with do. The clue is homework, which is a task you carry out, not something you create. So it is do their homework. Also, homework is uncountable: we don't say homeworks.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mis hijos hacen los deberes en la cocina.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My children make their homework in the kitchen.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence without the correction: homework goes with do.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My children do their homeworks in the kitchen.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb is correct, but homework is uncountable and does not take -s.

glosario.definicion_l: work, such as schoolwork or piecework, that is done at home

ejercicios.frase: He goes to home by train.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit says that home does not take to after go, come or get. The clue is goes to home: although we use to with other places (go to work), home works as an adverb and has no preposition. The correction is He goes home by train.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Go home does not take to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He goes to home by train.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence without the correction: go home does not take to.
The to is correctly removed, but with he the present simple needs -s: goes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He goes at home by train.
errores_previstos.explicacion: At home means “in your house”; it does not show movement towards the house.

ejercicios.explicacion: This unit says that adverbs of frequency go before the main verb. The clue is that the verb is walk, not be, so often goes between the subject and walk: I often walk to work. At the end of the sentence it is possible in speech, but it is not the neutral position.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The adverb of frequency goes before the main verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: A menudo voy andando al trabajo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The adverb doesn't go between the verb and its complement; it goes before the main verb.

glosario.definicion_l: many times at short intervals · frequently or in great quantities

respuestas: We never go to bed late
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit includes go to bed (lie down to sleep) and the rule that the adverb of frequency goes before the main verb. The order is subject (we), never, the verb and its fixed expression (go to bed), and late at the end. Never is already negative, so you don't add don't.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Never goes before the verb; go to bed means lie down to sleep.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We go never to bed late
errores_previstos.explicacion: Never goes before the main verb, not after it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We never go late to bed
errores_previstos.explicacion: Late doesn't go inside the fixed expression go to bed; it goes at the end.

glosario.definicion_l: not at all; certainly not; not in any circumstances; not ever; at no time in the past or future

ejercicios.explicacion: This unit gives get dressed (put on your clothes). The clue is get before the gap: the expression is get + the past participle dressed. It is not reflexive (we don't say dress themselves in a normal routine) and the past participle dressed does not change.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Put on your clothes is get dressed.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños se visten después del desayuno.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After get you need the past participle, dressed.
A calque of the Spanish reflexive “se visten”; get dressed does not take a pronoun.

ejercicios.frase: I usually ___ a shower before breakfast.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit includes have a shower; take a shower is also correct, especially in American English, but it is not one of the options. The clue is a shower: it is a fixed action with have, like meals. Make and do don't form this expression.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Wash under a shower is have (or take) a shower; make and do are wrong.
ejercicios.traduccion: Normalmente me ducho antes de desayunar.

por_opcion.have: Correct: have a shower (you can also say take a shower).
por_opcion.make: Incorrect: make a shower does not exist; make is used for creating something.
por_opcion.do: Incorrect: do does not go with shower.

descripcion_larga_es: This unit brings together the verbs and expressions to talk about a normal day: getting up, having a shower, eating, going to work, housework and free time, with adverbs of frequency. It is the first conversation topic at any level. It is difficult for Spanish speakers because many actions are fixed expressions with have, do, make or go (have breakfast, do the shopping, make the bed) that are not translated word for word.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of daily routine: verbs and phrasal verbs (wake up, get up, get dressed), fixed expressions with have, do, make and go, household tasks and free-time activities. It goes together with adverbs of frequency (always, usually, rarely, never) and the present simple, which is the tense we use to talk about habits.
contexto.por_que_importa: Saying what you do on a normal day is one of the most frequent tasks in a conversation and in speaking exams at basic and intermediate level. Collocation mistakes (make homework, take dinner, go to home) are very noticeable even if people understand you, and the position of the adverb of frequency quickly shows whether you know basic grammar.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When you introduce yourself, describe your week, or talk about your home or your hobbies. The signs are questions like “What do you usually do…?” or “What time do you…?”. Spanish speakers tend to always translate “hacer” as make and “tomar” as take, to put to before home and to put the adverb before be.
